alerts.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Arkansas,
including the following counties, in south central Arkansas,
Union. In southwest Arkansas, Columbia and Lafayette.

* WHEN...Until 345 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1246 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This will cause
urban and small stream flooding. While rainfall amounts have
been light over the last few hours, between 3 and 5 inches of
rain have fallen across the advisory area earlier this
morning.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to isolated 2 inches are
expected over the area through mid afternoon. This additional
rain will result in minor flooding. Should the heavy rain
areas expand or intensify, a Flash Flood Warning will be
needed.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
El Dorado, Magnolia, Smackover, Stamps, Waldo, Lewisville,
Norphlet, Junction City, McNeil, Bradley, Taylor, Calion,
Emerson, Buckner, Village, Atlanta, Mount Holly, Macedonia,
Lisbon and Smithland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

FFWSHV

The National Weather Service in Shreveport has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Union County in south central Arkansas...
Columbia County in southwestern Arkansas...
Eastern Lafayette County in southwestern Arkansas...
Northeastern Bossier Parish in northwestern Louisiana...
Claiborne Parish in northwestern Louisiana...
Webster Parish in northwestern Louisiana...

* Until 445 PM CDT.

* At 115 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
2 and in excess of 5 inches of rain have fallen since this
morning. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches, with
isolated higher amounts, are possible in the warned area through
late afternoon. Given that the grounds are saturated and this
additional rain will quickly run off, flash flooding is expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
El Dorado, Minden, Magnolia, Springhill, Homer, Smackover, Stamps,
Waldo, Norphlet, Junction City, McNeil, Haynesville, Cullen,
Cotton Valley, Sarepta, Bradley, Taylor, Calion, Emerson and
Buckner.

SVRSHV

The National Weather Service in Shreveport has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Union County in south central Arkansas...
Southeastern Columbia County in southwestern Arkansas...
Northwestern Union Parish in north central Louisiana...
Northeastern Claiborne Parish in northwestern Louisiana...

* Until 215 PM CDT.

* At 121 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
over Taylor to 9 miles north of Gibsland, or along a line from
near Springhill to 10 miles south of Homer, moving northeast at 55
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
El Dorado, Smackover, Norphlet, Huttig, Junction City, Strong,
Calion, Wesson, Lisbon, Lawson, Urbana, Mount Holly, Atlanta,
Village, Lapile, Calhoun, Spearsville, Lillie and Catesville.
